answer: One roll carries every velvet sheet a registered holder owns, and no identity acts without its stamped sheet. Each sheet must carry as many stamps as the roll holds sheets, one stranger per terrace, each stranger reading the whole roll and paid a measure of shale per sheet read. So the holder's k-th sheet costs k strangers and k squared measures of shale: a newcomer pays one stranger and one measure, while a holder of a thousand identities must line up five hundred thousand strangers and pay three hundred and thirty-three million measures.
